findings.title: previewRequiredPairs narrowed to AL-1 and AL-2 while previewScope was left byte-identical, so the artifact no longer states whether AL-3, AL-4 and AL-5 carry any first-slice obligation - including the bundle-promotion-gate test this row exists to force.
measured: previewScope is byte-identical to v2. firstSliceRequired still reads 'previewRequiredPairs. D-002 keeps DR-127 inside the slice. This contract does not defer the row.' It is a pointer, and its referent changed underneath it.
In v2 previewRequiredPairs was a surface-set sentence covering core, component and control at N and N+1. In v3 it is two tuples whose own 'proves' fields state 'AL-1' and 'AL-2' - and nothing else.

Field-by-field coverage of the five pass properties in v3: AL-1 and AL-2 have passProperty, conformance record, execution route, preview tuple and independentPublication record. AL-3, AL-4 and AL-5 have passProperty, conformance record and execution route, but no preview tuple and no first-slice statement anywhere in the artifact.

The live DR-127 row cell, byte-verified at file 08 line 309, names three design requirement groups: 'Bidirectional N/N+1 skew, independent rollback/coexistence, no bundle promotion gate'. PRP-AL1/PRP-AL2 discharge the first group. The second group is AL-3/AL-4 and the third is AL-5; neither now has a stated first-slice standing.
D-002 keeps DR-127 inside the condition-2 affected-row set, and the artifact itself repeats that in the very sentence at issue.
findings.whyItMatters: AL-5 is the bundle-is-not-a-hidden-promotion-gate property - the specific hazard this contract was commissioned to prevent, and the one file 11 pushes back on. After this repair the only field that says what the first slice requires resolves to two skew tuples that do not reach it. I do not read this as a deferral: nothing is deferred, no D-096 (A) grant is minted, and AL-3/AL-4/AL-5 keep their pass properties, conformance records and execution routes, so the substance survives elsewhere in the artifact. That is why this is a SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker. But a contract whose job is to state what DR-127 requires should not leave the first-slice standing of three of its five pass properties to inference, on a row file 08 marks 'Hard blocker for independent-release blueprint'.
findings.whatWouldClearIt: Update previewScope alongside previewRequiredPairs: state explicitly that AL-3, AL-4 and AL-5 are first-slice required at design level with their conformance records and named execution routes, and that previewRequiredPairs enumerates only the concrete N/N+1 skew tuples rather than the whole first-slice obligation. The sentence is self-limiting and therefore not a misroute, but saying plainly that DR-G16 has no accepted contract today would be truer than 'a reviewed owning gate'.
